label: Hormuz Traffic
change: Jul 16 (Day 139): Hormuz traffic effectively collapsed again after the MOU's 60-day safe-passage guarantee broke down — Jul 12 recorded only 10 transits vs. an ~88/day pre-crisis baseline; Jul 13 saw 14 transits (4 crude tankers), a ~60% weekly drop. US military escorted convoys moved 8M+ barrels through on one recent Sunday. Late Jun (MOU period): traffic had partially recovered to just over two dozen vessels/day (Jun 29) after the Jun 17 Islamabad MOU suspended Iran's per-vessel toll regime for 60 days — that recovery reversed after the Jul 6-7 tanker attack wave. Aug 12 (Day 166): Only 8 vessels transited Tuesday (Aug 11) vs. a 130-140/day pre-war rate and a ~12/day 10-day average, despite Trump's Aug 12 claim of 'total control' after minesweeping the strait. Aug 15-17 weekend: only 3-5 commercial ships transited all weekend. Aug 18-19 (Day 172-173): About 10 vessels transited Tuesday (Aug 18), roughly 90% below the pre-war baseline, as CENTCOM reported 64 vessels redirected, 3 disabled, and 2 boarded since the blockade was reimposed; 3 China-linked supertankers turned back mid-transit on Aug 19.
